purpose: Ablate persistent local surface-risk while retaining current-frame intrinsic-event mitigation, to test whether persistent risk memory is causal for the long residual trail.

interpretation.conclusion: Persistent local surface-risk is causal for long recovery duration: removing all local risk reads/writes cuts clear-to-5% from roughly 0.8 s to 66.7 ms and recovery p99 AUC by about 95%, while leaving the initial trail peak largely unchanged. Zero-memory event-only mode therefore breaks the ghost-duration tradeoff but undershoots the 0.70 weak-flash and 0.45 moving-flash gates. Next test should add only a tightly bounded 1-3-frame risk lifetime and stronger instantaneous gain, keeping production unchanged.
